value.text:
Eleven tackles a game, for 213 games, and two Defensive Player of the Year awards.

Taron Hayes played in the Kansas City secondary and played it like a linebacker. He made 2,418 tackles in his career, more than eleven every time he took the field, and he still found 30 interceptions along the way, one about every seven games. He was never credited with a sack or a forced fumble. He did his work in the open field, one ball carrier at a time.

The league named him Defensive Player of the Year twice. He never won a ring, and the Chiefs never needed to ask where he was on a Sunday. Among every defensive back the league has recorded, only three had a bigger career when he retired.

Taron Hayes, welcome to the Hall of Fame.
